shots.fix: Set y_range to start at 0 (e.g. [0,100]) or show a full bar chart with a visible axis so the bars read as a normal breakfast-glance chart. Title should be centred at the top, not left-aligned.

Move the 'Last year | This year' label away from the line so it doesn't overlap it, and stop the '98.50' bar label colliding with the point label. Label each bar separately ('Last year', 'This year'). Widen y_range (e.g. [98, 98.6]) so the bars look clearly tall vs. towering. Zoom out so the full bars show, and add the 'THE PUZZLE' title at top center, not top-left.

Frame is legible and the callout 'Check the axis' fits the 'something most people skip' line. To match the style, add a small off-centre visual such as a simple axis or graph with a brace or label, and move the text off-centre or beneath the visual. The centred text on an empty black canvas feels sparse.

Add visible y-axis tick labels (98.2 to 98.6) along the left side so 'numbers on the side' is shown. Make the bar value labels larger. Move the '98.2 and 98.6' label next to the axis and keep it clear of the line. Tighten the plot so the bars and line don't run off the frame, and bring the background closer to pure black.

Move the 'height 98.30' label so it does not overlap the '98.30' bar label. Add y-axis tick labels at 98.2 and 98.6 so the range is visible. Center the title at the top, and avoid the line running off the frame.

Enlarge the small bar labels (98.30, 98.50). The 98.50 label is clipped by the line and the yellow point, so move it clear. Add a bracket or label showing the 0.2 difference between the bars. Also darken the background to pure black to match the palette.

Fix the overlapping labels: the '98.50' bar label collides with the 'height 98.50' text and is clipped, and '98.30' touches the line. Offset the bar labels or drop the duplicate. Widen y_range so the bars and slope read as a small, harmless change, which better answers 'Does that look like a disaster?'. Also move the visual off-centre and add braces as the style calls for.

Zoom out so both bars and the full line are visible, and keep the bars at equal heights or mark them as unchanged. Move the label so it doesn't sit against the line. Center the title at the top, since it is currently top-left.

Move the callout off-centre or top-left and add a small axis graphic, such as a bar chart with a movable baseline, so it matches the layout and shows the 'moved' idea. Otherwise keep the emphasis on 'axis'.

The bars_at markers for 98.3 and 98.5 are missing; only a flat line at ~98.4 appears. Render the two bars or points so the tiny difference against the 0-based axis is visible. Also place the label top-left and keep the title centred in cyan to match the layout.

Render the two bars at 98.3 and 98.5 as distinct side-by-side bars (e.g. at x≈1 and x≈1.2), not a single horizontal line. Use a y_range like [95, 100] or add a zoom inset so the tiny height difference is visible, and move the 'Which is taller?' label off the line.

Style: the equation is centred and the frame is a bit sparse. Shift the visual off-centre or top-left and add a caption or brace labelling the 0.2 difference and the base of about 98, to match the layout description.

Add a visible bar object to the plot (for example, thick vertical bars at y=98.3 and y=98.5 with a highlighted segment) so it reads as a physical bar. The faint bars_at lines are barely visible. Also tie the label to the phrase, e.g. 'Bar as a physical object'. Make the title cyan and centred at the top per the style notes.

Text is readable, though the struck-through gray claim has low contrast against the dark background. Make the claim brighter, such as white, so the strikethrough stays legible. The style brief calls for an off-centre or top-left visual with braces and labels, and this centred text-only layout departs from it. Consider adding a small bar chart graphic with a brace labelled 3× and a 0.2% annotation, and use the yellow accent2 for the correction.

Callout text matches the phrase well (3× highlighted in cyan). To fit the style better, move the visual off-centre or top-left, add a visual such as a brace or label (3, R, dx) attached to it, and use a pure black background without the vignette gradient. Optionally change the header to match the cyan chapter-style titles.

Add the bars_at markers at 98.3 and 98.5 with small labels, plus a y-axis tick at 98.2, so it's clear the plot starts at the floor and only the part above is drawn. Move the 'Floor: 98.2' label next to the line, and put a title in light cyan at top center to match the style.

The plot shows only a flat line at 98.4 with no bars at 98.3 and 98.5, so the 0.1 and 0.3 leftovers are not visible. Make the bars_at markers render, and add labeled braces showing 0.1 and 0.3 against the line. Move the label out of the top-right corner and place it beside the plot. Brighten the vertical axis and gridlines.

Show the morph mid-transition, or keep the 0.3/0.1 = 3 side visible, so the '3 to one' ratio of leftovers appears next to 98.5/98.3 ≈ 1.002. Also move the visual off-centre to match the layout, add a label or brace on the leftover 0.3, and match the accent highlight to the '3'.

Show the phrase's point: add a labeled marker or bar at 98.2 (e.g. bars_at [98.2]) and put a '98.2' tick label on the y-axis. Currently the line sits at 98.4 with no 98.2 marker, and 'Floor: 97.8' is unrelated to the phrase. Change the label to something like '98.2: nothing special'. Add more y-axis ticks (98.0, 98.2, 98.4) and make the bars visible.

Show the truncated y-axis effect: add tick labels (98.3, 98.5) and the bars_at markers so the flat line at 98.4 is visibly bounded, and add a small wiggle or change to the function (e.g. fn '98.4 + 0.05*sin(x)') so a small change looks exaggerated. Move the title to the top center in cyan.

The frame shows only the end state 'skyrocket', so the morph from '0.2 wobble' is lost. Capture the mid-morph or show both terms, e.g. keep '0.2 wobble' visible beside or above 'skyrocket'. Move the visual off-centre and add a caption, as the style calls for.

The frame shows only a flat line labeled 'Three bars', with no actual bars drawn. Render three visible bars at 98.3 (filled, or with distinct x-positions) so the label matches. Add a small caption such as 'no arithmetic needed' to tie it to the phrase. Move the title to the centered top in light cyan, per the layout.

Make the ruler read as a ruler: add tick marks or a wooden-style rectangle laid along the y-axis instead of a horizontal line spanning the x-axis. Move the 'height 98.30' label away from the axis tick labels and the top edge. Add a chapter-style title, and keep the cyan and yellow accents.

Mark zero explicitly with a highlighted tick or 'zero' label at the origin, and show a visible bar from 0 up to 98.3, e.g. a thick filled bar or a bracket along its length, rather than a flat horizontal line. Move the 'height 98.30' label away from the y-axis tick numbers so it doesn't crowd them.

Render the three bars (bars_at 98.3) so they are visible and rest on a y-axis starting at 0. Add a marker showing the ruler's end at the base. Move the 'height 98.30' label off the axis tick labels, and set the y_range tick marks to match the data.

Show the bars (bars_at: 98.3 x3) as filled columns with a visible movable baseline, e.g. a yellow line rising past the bar bottoms, and color the sawed-off portion distinctly. Add y-axis ticks (98, 98.3, 98.6) so the 'climbing edge' reads, and move the 'Chunk sawed off' label next to the cut region.

Show a visible ruler or bracket spanning the chunk (e.g. a brace from 0 to 98 with a label) instead of only a flat line. The 'bars_at' markers don't render, so the chunk size isn't clear. Add a vertical brace/bars at the interval ends, and make the axis text a bit larger. The title should be centered at the top, not left-aligned.
Shift the equation off-centre or top-left and add a bar visual with a brace labeled 98.3 and a highlighted 98 segment, so the 'nearly all of it' idea is pictured rather than just written.

Show the truncated axis (90-100) next to a full 0-100 bar so the sliver is visible against the whole bar. Right now only a thin horizontal line appears, with no bars and no contrast with the full bar.

The shot props specify bars_at [40, 72, 95], but no bars appear in the frame, so add them or remove the prop. Move the label to a centered cyan title, and show a different chart with a clearer contrast to the prior one.

Move the equation off-centre or top-left and add a bar visual with a brace and label beside it. Keep the 'length' highlight in cyan.

Add axis ticks or a stock-price y-axis label so it reads as a stock chart. Raise the grid contrast. Move the 'Two weeks' label closer to the line, or place it as a brace under the x-axis. Shift the line up so it isn't pressed against the bottom edge.

Title is not centred at the top as the layout requires: move 'THE RULE' to the centre in light cyan. Also brighten the faint y-axis labels and gridlines, and drop the small upturn at the right edge (or make it clearly intentional).

Make the sliver clearer: zoom the x_range to about [490, 520] or highlight the final segment so the tiny uptick is visible. Add a label for the two weeks. Replace the half-ellipse plot with a 3D pie visual: a tilted ellipse with a highlighted front slice nearer the viewer. Move the label to the top-left or beside the visual. Remove the flat extension lines and axis clutter, and add a thin white frame around the scene.

Enlarge the nodes or shrink the font so labels fit inside the circles. 'Misleading size', 'Truncated axis' and 'Zoomed window' are clipped at the circle edges. Use shorter labels or widen the nodes.

Frame matches the phrase well. To fit the style better, move the list off-centre or top-left, center the title in light cyan at the top, and add a small visual such as a labeled diagram beside the bullets.

Raise the contrast of the struck-through claim, since the gray text on black is dim. Add a small visual such as a chart icon to fill the empty space and match the off-centre layout. The background looks like a dark teal gradient rather than pure black, so change it to #000000.

Optionally move the callout off-centre or top-left and add a small visual such as a thermometer, since the palette calls for an off-centre visual and this frame is text only. The text itself works as is.

Center the 'ONE SUBTLETY' title at the top rather than left-aligned. Add a brace or label on the trend, for example a dashed upward trend line, to show that the trend persists. Move the label beside the curve instead of the top-right corner.
